summary.text: A beneficiary may claim up to $6,000 from the deceased’s un-nominated CPF monies for funeral expenses.

details.heading: How much can be claimed
details.body: Generally, claims of up to $6,000 are allowable.

details.heading: Relationship documents
details.body: The document needed depends on whether you are the spouse, child, parent or sibling of the deceased.

details.heading: How payment is made
details.body: Payment is made by PayNow or direct credit to a bank account. PayNow must be registered with your NRIC.

steps.name: Check that you can claim
steps.text: You must be a beneficiary of the deceased to claim reimbursement of funeral expenses from the deceased’s un-nominated CPF monies.

steps.name: Apply for the amount
steps.text: In the online application form, indicate the amount of funeral expenses you want to claim.

steps.name: Gather your documents
steps.text: Prepare the documents that show your relationship to the deceased, the Declaration Form for funeral expenses, and the relevant funeral receipts.

steps.name: Submit the claim
steps.text: Submit the required supporting documents, including the Declaration Form and relevant receipts for funeral expenses.

example_phrasings: what help is there to pay for a funeral

sources.page_title: How can I claim for reimbursement of funeral expenses out of the deceased's un-nominated CPF monies?

quotes.text: Generally, claims of up to $6,000 are allowable.
Only a beneficiary is eligible to claim for reimbursement of funeral expenses from the deceased's un-nominated CPF monies.
You can indicate the amount of funeral expenses which you would like to claim from the deceased's un-nominated CPF monies in the online application form.
The claimant will have to submit the following supporting documents:
Relevant receipts incurred for Funeral Expenses.
Payment will be made to the claimant via PayNow (which has to be registered with your NRIC) or Direct Credit to the bank account.
